questions_and_answers.question_text: Where are the boundaries of běifāng and nánfāng in China?
Why can't pǔtōnghuà be equated with Běijīng huà?
What term is used in Taiwan instead?
When is shi necessary after bù zhǐ, and when may it be omitted?

answers.answer_text: The area between the Huáng Hé (Yellow River) and the Chángjiāng (Yangtze River).

questions_and_answers.question_text: Write the Chinese for "Northerners like to eat foods made from wheat, and southerners like to eat rice."

answers.answer_text: Běifāng rén xǐhuan chī miànshí, nánfāng rén xǐhuan chī mǐfàn.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Are Běijīng's own regional expressions considered pǔtōnghuà?

answers.answer_text: No — purely regional expressions, including those of Běijīng itself, are not considered pǔtōnghuà.

questions_and_answers.question_text: What did pǔtōnghuà mean before the PRC?

answers.answer_text: The approximations of Mandarin spoken by the common people of northern China.

questions_and_answers.question_text: Give two alternatives to bù zhǐ shi.

answers.answer_text: Any two of: bú dàn shi, bù guāng shi, bù jǐn shi.

articles.text:
5. A: Dàbùfen běifāng rén dōu huì    Most northerners can speak the standard
      shuō pǔtōnghuà, duì bu duì?    language, can't they?
   B: Ou, bù zhǐ shi běifāng rén,   Oh, not just northerners. A lot of
      hěn duō nánfāng rénde          southerners speak standard Chinese
      pǔtōnghuà yě bú cuò.           pretty well, too.

Notes on No. 5

Běifāng, "the north" of a country, and nánfāng, "the south." When used of China, these usually mean the area NORTH OF THE HUÁNG HÉ (Yellow River) and the area SOUTH OF THE CHÁNGJIĀNG (Yangtze River), respectively. The area BETWEEN the rivers is usually considered CENTRAL China.

Běifāng rén xǐhuan chī miànshí,  Northerners like to eat foods made from
nánfāng rén xǐhuan chī mǐfàn.    wheat, and southerners like to eat rice.

pǔtōnghuà: "the common speech," the usual designation in the PRC for what we have called "Standard Chinese." Pǔtōnghuà is OFFICIALLY DEFINED as consisting of:
  — the SOUND SYSTEM of Běijīng speech,
  — the VOCABULARY and IDIOM of northern speech, and
  — the GRAMMAR of exemplary modern vernacular writings.

It would be INACCURATE to equate pǔtōnghuà with either běifāng huà ("northern speech") or Běijīng huà ("Běijīng speech"), because pǔtōnghuà has ABSORBED many elements from other dialects. Conversely, purely REGIONAL expressions (including those of Běijīng itself) and NON-STANDARD pronunciations are NOT considered pǔtōnghuà.

Before the PRC, the term pǔtōnghuà already existed, but referred to the approximations of Mandarin spoken by the common people of northern China. (In Taiwan, the term GUÓYǓ, "the national language," is used.)

bù zhǐ shi běifāng rén: "not just northerners." Bù zhǐ shi, "not only," can be followed by a NOUN, VERB, or CLAUSE. You may also hear bù jiǔ shi, bú dàn shi, bù guāng shi, or bù jǐn shi. The SHI is NECESSARY before a noun but may be OMITTED before a verb.

Wǒmen bàngōngshì bù zhǐ (shi)    In our office, there are not only
yǒu Měiguó rén, hái yǒu jǐge     Americans, but also some Chinese who
Zhōngguó rén bāng wǒmen gōngzuò. help us.
